Below are a few ways you can grab a screenshot of a web page **using Python**.  
Pick the one that best matches what you’re trying to do:

| Goal | Recommended tool | Why |
|------|------------------|-----|
| **Take a screenshot of a *specific* URL** (no need to interact with an already‑open Chrome window) | **Selenium + ChromeDriver** (or **pyppeteer** / **Playwright**) | Full control over the browser, headless or headed, can capture full‑page screenshots, take screenshots after scrolling, etc. |
| **Capture whatever is currently visible in an *already‑open* Chrome window** (e.g. you’re browsing manually and want to snapshot the tab you’re looking at) | **pyautogui** or **mss** (screen‑capture libraries) | These grab pixels from the OS display, so they’ll capture exactly what you see on screen, regardless of the browser’s internal state. |
| **Use Chrome DevTools Protocol directly** | **pychrome** or **chrome-devtools-protocol** | Useful if you already have a Chrome instance running with remote debugging enabled (`chrome --remote-debugging-port=9222`). |

Below are code snippets for each scenario.  
Feel free to copy‑paste, tweak, and run them in your environment.

---

## 1️⃣ Screenshot a URL with Selenium (Chrome)

# pip install selenium chromedriver-autoinstaller
import chromedriver_autoinstaller
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.service import Service
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options

# Make sure the ChromeDriver binary matches your Chrome version
chromedriver_autoinstaller.install()  # installs to ~/.local/bin/chromedriver

chrome_options = Options()
chrome_options.add_argument("--headless")          # run without UI
chrome_options.add_argument("--disable-gpu")
chrome_options.add_argument("--window-size=1920,1080")  # set viewport size

service = Service()
driver = webdriver.Chrome(service=service, options=chrome_options)

try:
    driver.get("https://www.example.com")

    # Optional: wait for page to fully load
    driver.implicitly_wait(10)
